questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice: 'Ali wrote an essay yesterday.'

options.A: An essay was written by Ali yesterday.
options.B: An essay had been written by Ali yesterday.
options.C: An essay is written by Ali yesterday.
options.D: An essay has been written by Ali yesterday.

questions.explanation: Past simple tense in active voice ('wrote') changes into 'was/were + past participle' ('was written') in passive voice.

questions.question: Select the correct active voice of: 'The car is being washed by the driver.'

options.A: The driver washes the car.
options.B: The driver was washing the car.
options.C: The driver is washing the car.
options.D: The driver has washed the car.

questions.explanation: 'is being washed' is present continuous passive, which corresponds to the present continuous active form 'is washing'.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is in the PASSIVE voice?

options.A: The gardener pruned the rose bushes this morning.
options.B: The committee has evaluated all applications.
options.C: The historical monument was restored by renowned architects.
options.D: The birds will migrate south before winter.

questions.explanation: Option C features the passive auxiliary 'was restored' with the agent introduced by the prepositional phrase 'by renowned architects'.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice: 'The students are preparing a science exhibition.'

options.A: A science exhibition was being prepared by the students.
options.B: A science exhibition is prepared by the students.
options.C: A science exhibition is being prepared by the students.
options.D: A science exhibition has been prepared by the students.

questions.explanation: Present continuous active ('are preparing') converts to 'is/am/are being + past participle' ('is being prepared').

questions.question: Select the correct passive voice: 'They had announced the results before sunset.'

options.A: The results have been announced by them before sunset.
options.B: The results had been announced by them before sunset.
options.C: The results were announced by them before sunset.
options.D: The results had announced before sunset.

questions.explanation: Past perfect active ('had announced') changes into 'had been + past participle' ('had been announced') in passive voice.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice of the imperative sentence: 'Open the window.'

options.A: Let the window be opened.
options.B: The window must open.
options.C: Let the window open.
options.D: You open the window.

questions.explanation: Imperative commands are converted into passive using the formula: 'Let + object + be + past participle' ('Let the window be opened').

questions.question: Convert into passive voice: 'Do not pluck the flowers.'

options.A: Let the flowers not be plucked.
options.B: The flowers are not to pluck.
options.C: Let not flowers be pluck.
options.D: Flowers should not pluck.

questions.explanation: Negative imperatives take the passive form 'Let + object + not + be + past participle' ('Let the flowers not be plucked').

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice: 'Who broke this mirror?'

options.A: By whom was this mirror broken?
options.B: By who was this mirror broken?
options.C: Whom broke this mirror?
options.D: By whom this mirror was broken?

questions.explanation: Interrogative sentences with 'Who' change to 'By whom + auxiliary verb + subject + past participle' ('By whom was this mirror broken?').

questions.question: Select the correct passive voice: 'Why did you punish him?'

options.A: Why was he punished by you?
options.B: Why did he be punished by you?
options.C: Why he was punished by you?
options.D: Why had he been punished by you?

questions.explanation: In past simple interrogative passive, 'Why did you punish him?' becomes 'Why was he punished by you?' maintaining inversion (auxiliary 'was' before subject 'he').

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice: 'We must respect our teachers.'

options.A: Our teachers must be respected by us.
options.B: Our teachers must respected by us.
options.C: Our teachers have to be respected by us.
options.D: Our teachers are respected by us.

questions.explanation: Modal auxiliary 'must' transforms into 'modal + be + past participle' ('must be respected').

questions.question: Select the correct passive voice: 'She can solve this mathematical problem.'

options.A: This mathematical problem can be solved by her.
options.B: This mathematical problem could be solved by her.
options.C: This mathematical problem can solve by her.
options.D: This mathematical problem is solved by her.

questions.explanation: Modal auxiliary 'can' takes 'can be + past participle' ('can be solved') in passive voice; the tense of the modal does not change.

questions.question: Which of the following verbs CANNOT be converted into passive voice?

options.A: Destroy
options.B: Sleep
options.C: Write
options.D: Build

questions.explanation: 'Sleep' is an intransitive verb; intransitive verbs cannot take a direct object and therefore cannot be converted into the passive voice.

questions.question: Select the passive voice: 'The principal gave the boy a scholarship.' (Focusing on the recipient)

options.A: The boy was given a scholarship by the principal.
options.B: A scholarship had been given to the boy by the principal.
options.C: The boy was giving a scholarship by the principal.
options.D: A scholarship was gave by the principal to the boy.

questions.explanation: When a sentence has both an indirect object ('the boy') and direct object ('a scholarship'), either may be the subject; here 'The boy was given a scholarship by the principal' correctly promotes the indirect object.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice: 'They will have finished the bridge by December.'

options.A: The bridge will have been finished by them by December.
options.B: The bridge will be finished by them by December.
options.C: The bridge would have been finished by them by December.
options.D: The bridge will has been finished by them by December.

questions.explanation: Future perfect active ('will have finished') changes to 'will have been + past participle' ('will have been finished').

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice of the sentence with prepositional verb: 'They laughed at the clown.'

options.A: The clown was laughed at by them.
options.B: The clown was laughed by them.
options.C: The clown had been laughed at by them.
options.D: The clown laughed at them.

questions.explanation: In prepositional verbs ('laughed at'), the preposition must be retained alongside the past participle in passive voice ('was laughed at by them').

questions.question: Select the correct passive voice: 'The nurse is looking after the orphan.'

options.A: The orphan is being looked after by the nurse.
options.B: The orphan was being looked after by the nurse.
options.C: The orphan is looked after by the nurse.
options.D: The orphan has been looked after by the nurse.

questions.explanation: Present continuous with prepositional verb: 'is looking after' -> 'is being looked after by'.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice: 'People speak English all over the world.'

options.A: English is spoken all over the world.
options.B: English was spoken all over the world.
options.C: English has been spoken by people all over the world.
options.D: English is being spoken all over the world.

questions.explanation: When the agent is vague or understood ('people'), the by-phrase is typically omitted: 'English is spoken all over the world'.

questions.question: Select the correct passive voice: 'Someone has stolen my bicycle.'

options.A: My bicycle has been stolen.
options.B: My bicycle was stolen by someone.
options.C: My bicycle had been stolen.
options.D: My bicycle is stolen.

questions.explanation: Indefinite pronouns ('someone', 'somebody') are omitted in passive voice: 'My bicycle has been stolen'.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice: 'Rose smells sweet.'

options.A: Rose is sweet when it is smelt.
options.B: Rose was smelt sweet.
options.C: Rose is smelt by everyone sweet.
options.D: Sweetness is smelled by the rose.

questions.explanation: Quasi-passive sensory verbs take the formula: 'Subject + be + adjective + when it is + past participle' ('Rose is sweet when it is smelt').

questions.question: Select the correct passive voice: 'Quinine tastes bitter.'

options.A: Quinine is bitter when it is tasted.
options.B: Quinine was tasted bitter.
options.C: Bitter is tasted by quinine.
options.D: Quinine tastes bitterly when eaten.

questions.explanation: Middle/quasi-passive verbs like 'taste' become 'Quinine is bitter when it is tasted'.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice: 'One should keep one's promises.'

options.A: Promises should be kept.
options.B: One's promises should be kept by one.
options.C: Promises must keep by one.
options.D: Promises are to be kept by someone.

questions.explanation: When 'one' is used as an impersonal subject, the by-phrase 'by one' is omitted: 'Promises should be kept'.

questions.question: Convert into passive voice: 'Please help me.'

options.A: You are requested to help me.
options.B: Let me be helped by you.
options.C: I should be helped please.
options.D: Help must be given to me.

questions.explanation: Polite requests using 'Please' are appropriately converted into 'You are requested to + infinitive' ('You are requested to help me').

questions.question: Select the correct passive voice: 'Work hard.'

options.A: You are advised to work hard.
options.B: Let hard work be done.
options.C: Hard work should done by you.
options.D: You must work hard.

questions.explanation: Intransitive imperative sentences expressing advice are converted using 'You are advised to + infinitive' ('You are advised to work hard').

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice: 'They proposed a new educational policy.'

options.A: A new educational policy was proposed by them.
options.B: A new educational policy had been proposed by them.
options.C: A new educational policy is proposed by them.
options.D: A new educational policy has been proposed.

questions.explanation: Past simple active ('proposed') becomes 'was proposed by them' in passive voice.

questions.question: Select the correct passive voice: 'Did the police arrest the culprit?'

options.A: Was the culprit arrested by the police?
options.B: Did the culprit be arrested by the police?
options.C: Had the culprit been arrested by the police?
options.D: Is the culprit arrested by the police?

questions.explanation: Past simple Yes/No questions change from 'Did + subject + V1' to 'Was/Were + subject + V3' ('Was the culprit arrested by the police?').

questions.question: Convert into active voice: 'The match was won by the national team.'

options.A: The national team won the match.
options.B: The national team wins the match.
options.C: The national team has won the match.
options.D: The national team was winning the match.

questions.explanation: 'was won' is past simple passive, converting back into past simple active 'won'.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice: 'The earthquake destroyed hundreds of houses.'

options.A: Hundreds of houses were destroyed by the earthquake.
options.B: Hundreds of houses had been destroyed by the earthquake.
options.C: Hundreds of houses was destroyed by the earthquake.
options.D: Hundreds of houses are destroyed by the earthquake.

questions.explanation: 'Hundreds of houses' is plural, requiring the plural auxiliary 'were': 'were destroyed by the earthquake'.

questions.question: Which tense NEVER has a standard passive form in English?

options.A: Present Perfect Continuous
options.B: Past Continuous
options.C: Future Simple
options.D: Present Simple

questions.explanation: In standard English grammar, the four tenses that do not have recognized passive forms are: Present Perfect Continuous, Past Perfect Continuous, Future Continuous, and Future Perfect Continuous.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice: 'The mechanic has repaired the engine.'

options.A: The engine has been repaired by the mechanic.
options.B: The engine was repaired by the mechanic.
options.C: The engine had been repaired by the mechanic.
options.D: The engine is repaired by the mechanic.

questions.explanation: Present perfect active ('has repaired') transforms into 'has been + past participle' ('has been repaired').

questions.question: Select the correct passive voice: 'Do not tell a lie.'

options.A: Let a lie not be told.
options.B: A lie is not told.
options.C: Let not a lie told.
options.D: You do not tell a lie.

questions.explanation: Negative imperative passive follows 'Let + object + not + be + V3' ('Let a lie not be told').

questions.question: Select the correct active voice of: 'A delicious meal was being prepared by chef Tariq.'

options.A: Chef Tariq was preparing a delicious meal.
options.B: Chef Tariq prepared a delicious meal.
options.C: Chef Tariq is preparing a delicious meal.
options.D: Chef Tariq had prepared a delicious meal.

questions.explanation: 'was being prepared' is past continuous passive, which converts back to past continuous active 'was preparing'.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice: 'I know him very well.'

options.A: He is known to me very well.
options.B: He is known by me very well.
options.C: He was known to me very well.
options.D: He has been known by me very well.

questions.explanation: The past participle 'known' takes the preposition 'to' rather than 'by' in passive constructions: 'He is known to me very well'.

questions.question: Select the correct passive voice: 'His behavior surprised everyone.'

options.A: Everyone was surprised at his behavior.
options.B: Everyone was surprised by his behavior.
options.C: Everyone was surprised to his behavior.
options.D: Everyone had been surprised with his behavior.

questions.explanation: The verb 'surprised' in passive voice typically pairs with the preposition 'at' when referring to conduct or actions ('surprised at his behavior').

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice: 'The smoke filled the room.'

options.A: The room was filled with smoke.
options.B: The room was filled by smoke.
options.C: The room had been filled of smoke.
options.D: The room is filled with smoke.

questions.explanation: The verb 'filled' takes the preposition 'with' in passive voice ('filled with smoke') rather than 'by'.

questions.question: Convert into active voice: 'The project will be completed by the team next week.'

options.A: The team will complete the project next week.
options.B: The team would complete the project next week.
options.C: The team will have completed the project next week.
options.D: The team completes the project next week.

questions.explanation: 'will be completed' is future simple passive, which translates back to future simple active 'will complete'.
